title: MLINE-referenced LTYPE with ordered multi-chunk binary XDATA

scope.source: Runtime-generated LTYPE, APPID and reference records; no repository drawing fixture was added.
scope.cross_product: Both source encodings were exported to both output encodings.
scope.linetype: EditDash, two simple dash segments [1.0, -0.5], declared length 1.5, source flags 0, alignment 65.

xdata_profiles.purpose: Exercise the documented maximum 127-byte group-1004 chunk followed by a second chunk.
Distinguish ordered chunk boundaries and exact 2/3/3-byte payload preservation.

authority.relevant_rule: XDATA group 1004 carries binary data in chunks of at most 127 bytes; ASCII DXF represents the bytes as hexadecimal digits.

proof.source: Generated ASCII/binary input is checked as physical ordered 1001/1004 groups and freshly imported typed XDATA; each typed chunk must match its authored source chunk exactly.
proof.output: The staged output proof checks exact group order, chunk count and hex bytes, APPID provider fields/owner, and fresh typed readback for each source/output encoding pair.
proof.failure_retry: For each profile and encoding pair, removing the required APPID provider refuses without replacing a destination sentinel; restoring the provider succeeds on the same adapter and rechecks exact physical and typed output.

validation.asan: NOT_RUN; this slice changes generated test profiles and does not modify production allocation, ownership, lifetime or parser behavior.

limits: The two exact selected chunk layouts are qualified. Alternate byte values, chunk counts/orderings and chunk-boundary compositions remain unqualified.
Malformed hex, odd-length payloads, and a single 128-byte group-1004 chunk are not tested by this slice.

The receipt proves selected field transport and retry behavior only; it does not establish application-specific XDATA meaning, native MLINE rendering, recursive document closure, broader LTYPE support or a format-support claim.
